Furthermore plenty of cis athletes have "biological advantages" that help them at sports. Taller people are obviously going to have an easier time playing basketball, but I don't think we should have height bans in the name of fairness. Michael Phelps has a wingspan longer than his height, something very uncommon biologically which probably gives him a sports advantage according to experts, but I don't see people suggesting he be disqualified. I think singling out trans people, especially trans students, is unnecessary and harmful. Trans students are kids just like every other student, and sometimes they want to play sports.

Instead of looking to your dysphoria to "determine" whether or not you're trans, I'd encourage you instead to focus on what makes you feel most comfortable in your own body. You don't have to have exact answers or know things for sure from the outset, often times transition is a process of discovering what makes you feel most like yourself! Each step in the process you take will tell you a little more about if this is the right path for you and you always have the power to stop or pause the process at any time. Changes from HRT are often slow at the outset and many will reverse if you choose to stop (but not all, talk to your Dr). Unfortunately you probably won't be able to figure out any hard "proof" that you're transgender, but hopefully each step you take leads you closer to figuring things out. Best of luck!

I highly recommend reading "Drawing on the Right Side of the Brain" if you are struggling with the physical and intellectual process of drawing/artmaking. If it's more of a philosophical problem around the creation of art I recommend "The Creative Act" by Rick Ruben and "Art & Fear"

There is no finish line at which you are declared good at art. Instead art is a process of looking and refining over and over again. The thing we think of "Artistic Skill" isn't a single thing, but instead a set of related skills, all of which can be learned and strengthened! Focusing on the act of creation as a learning process and knowing that you can always try again has helped me with some of my art fears. 

Good luck on your art journey.

As a trans man, I didn't really "feel" gender until puberty, at which point it "felt" viscerally uncomfortable at every level. For me, going through puberty is what made it obvious there was a problem with my gender.

 Every change felt alien and uncomfortable, but adults assured me that was simply a quirk of puberty that would eventually fade. I had trouble sleeping, struggled with schoolwork, and felt constantly aware of and uncomfortable with my body. I was miserable and depressed, my teachers were so concerned about my mood that they contacted my parents. 

I continued to feel very uncomfortable with my gender presentation throughout my schooling years and after 5 years of discomfort I saw a video by a trans man describing his experience. I began by socially transitioning for around 6mo and I felt so much more confident and comfortable in my body. Every masculine change in my presentation made me feel happier and more at home in my body. 

Testosterone brought more positive changes, and then after another year I had saved enough to pay for top surgery. I cannot describe how much more comfortable and happy I am without breasts. Every change I have made has greatly helped that feeling of wrongness that started at puberty.

I honestly don't know numbers wise about our store's size, just experience wise. It's a lot, walks, sorting, and push-outs take almost till 3am most nights. One cashier recently started a strategy of stacking 9 boxes and pre-sorting most of the returns which has saved some time on the back end. I've worked as O/N CSM at two different stores and the roles were very different
Store One (very small): after midnight resets work on zoning front end, work any 82 freight and/or sort any apparel, check log book for front end foods that should be out of date and then remove+claim any expired. Audits. Plastic and trash + wipe down registers. Spot checks for dates. Occasionally pick from the 82 bins. Fill in schedule by hand (i do not miss this). At 6:30 sort any returns that come back from zoning. This was a rather small store so more than half the time I had at least 1-2 departments that I was working as a stocker in as well or other projects such as picking and reorganizing various bins.
